question.leadin: A palace in this city contains portraits of all of its rulers except one, whose portrait was replaced by a black sheet as punishment for treason.
question.text: Name this Italian city at the end of the Adriatic Sea which was a merchant republic ruled by doges such as Enrico Dandolo and dominated Mediterranean commerce for centuries.
question.answerHtml: the Most Serene Republic of Venice [or Venezia, or La Serenissimà]
question.answer: the Most Serene Republic of Venice
question.clue: This republic's leaders participated in the annual "Marriage of the Sea" ceremony using the ceremonial raft Bucentaur.

swap.leadin: Name these Italian cities important to Renaissance politics.
swap.text: This Tuscan city suffered the 1378 Ciompi Revolt, and the crazed monk Savonarola ousted a dynasty in this city founded by banker Cosimo di Medici.
swap.clue: This Tuscan city traditionally rivaled Pisa before conquering it in 1406.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Italy during World War II.
question.text: A member of the House of Savoy, this man saw the rise and fall of Mussolini during his reign as King of Italy.
question.clue: This King of Italy handed power to Mussolini following the March on Rome, and declared an armistice with the Allies in 1943; following the war, he abdicated the throne to his son.

swap.leadin: In 415 BCE, an expedition of over 100 triremes [tri-reems] sailed to this island to attack the city of Syracuse.
swap.text: Name this island off the coast of Italy.
swap.clue: Mamertines who moved to this island helped cause the First Punic War by asking Rome for aid.

question.leadin: Answer the following about powerful Italian families during the Renaissance.
question.text: The excesses of the Italian Borgia family were targeted by this Dominican Friar who organized the 1497 Bonfire of the Vanities.
question.clue: He increased his authority by predicting the invasion of Charles VIII, and the Arrabbiati formed in opposition to him.

swap.text: This massive Italian ship collided in 1956 with the MS Stockholm just off the coast of Massachusetts, and sank eleven hours later. Almost all of the deaths came from the initial collision.
swap.clue: This man, the primary target of the Fieschi conspiracy, was depicted as the god Neptune by Agnolo Bronzino.

question.text: Francis I was locked in the Pizzighettone ("Peet-see-get-TOH-nay") and forced to sign the Treaty of Madrid after being captured by Charles V at this 1525 battle during the Italian Wars.
question.clue: The final active Yorkist pretender to the English throne, Richard de la Pole, was killed at this battle.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about European universities.
swap.text: This university is the oldest in continual operation in the world, having been founded in 1088. It is the second largest in its country behind La Sapienza and was the first place to use the term "universitas."
swap.clue: This Italian university where Bettisia Gozzadini was the first woman in history to receive a degree. This university in Emilia-Romagna is the oldest continuously operating college in the world.

question.text: Engineered by Peter III of Aragon, it was ended by the Peace of Caltabellota, which put Frederick III on the throne. For 15 points, name this conflict, begun during the ringing of bells for a liturgical hour, in which Angevin rule of a Mediteranean island ended.
question.clue: That king attempted to end this conflict by challenging Peter III of Aragon to personal combat with Edward I serving as the judge of the contest.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about banking in Renaissance Italy.
swap.text: This city's Bank of St. George was opened in 1407 to manage public debt. Bank officials, in lieu of city administrators, directly governed this city's colonies of Corsica and Caffa.
swap.clue: A territory ruled by this city was attacked in 1553 by a joint Franco-Ottoman force under Turgut Reis.

question.text: Among Cavour's tasks was controlling Francesco Crispi and this man, a former Carbonari, and the military leader of the Italian unification.
question.clue: This leader of the Red Shirts who overthrew the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about Italian independence.
swap.text: This kingdom, ruled by Victor Emmanuel II, provided the impetus for Italian independence by becoming a prominent actor in world affairs as a response to Austrian dominance.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the career of Pope Sixtus IV.
question.text: Sixtus' nephew Giralamo Riario was advanced as the candidate to take the place of Lorenzo de Medici as part of this failed 1478 conspiracy.
question.clue: Frederico Montelfeltro likely had a battalion waiting in the hills during this event, which left citizens hanging from the walls of the Palazzo Vecchio and tossed into the Arno river.

swap.text: The exclusion of non-guild members from civic government led to this 14th-century uprising of textile workers in Florence. The wool carder Michele di Lando and the so-called "Eight Saints" led this three-year revolt.
swap.clue: Precipitated by the dominance of the Albizi family and the lack of a response from the Signoria, those who took part in this event were led by such men as Luigi di Guiccciardini and Michele di Lando.

question.text: Contrasting with the large-scale T-O maps of the three continents are these medieval maps of coastlines which are constructed using a network of rhumblines radiating from compasses spread around the map.
question.clue: The Beinecke also keeps many of these late medieval maps, which used known distances between coastal cities and straight "rhumb lines" along compass directions to draw the Mediterranean and other sea outlines extremely accurately.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about leagues in European history.
swap.text: This 1508 league was organized by Julius II against Venice, but the pope flip-flopped and allied with Venice later, proclaiming a "Holy League" against France.
swap.clue: Its opponent blamed the defeat on the indecisive leadership of Leonardo Loredan, which was thought to have contributed to the loss at Agnadello.

question.text: Ferdinand II intervened in Italy to defend his family's interest in this Italian kingdom. This kingdom later merged with Sicily to form the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
question.clue: With Milan and Sardinia, this kingdom was transferred from Spain to Austria by the War of the Spanish Succession.

swap.text: After retiring, Cassiodorus founded this monastery on his property in Squillace ("squee-LAH-chay") near the Castellum. While at this monastery, whose name means "fishpond," Cassiodorus wrote the encyclopedic handbook Institutes.

question.text: This chief of staff of the Italian Army lost his position to Armando Diaz after getting his ass handed to him at Caporetto.
question.clue: This Italian general from World War I who was dismissed after his army was shoved back at the Battle of Caporetto.

swap.leadin: You, Ted Gioia, and a time machine. Join the thuggish Gioia clan and answer these questions about one of the two Sicilies.
swap.text: This Norman kicked the Byzantines out of Italy in 1071 and died while on a bender in the Greek islands sieging Cephallonia.
swap.clue: This man, who spent three years besieging the city of Bari, died on the island of Kefalonia after he rescued Gregory VII from the Castel Sant' Angelo during Henry IV's siege of Rome.
